messages:
Maria Gomez: Heads up — noticed a sustained egress telemetry spike from eu-west dedicated pool during the tenant handoff window 08:12-08:18 UTC. Spikes coincide with a flurry of `SVC_HANDSHAKE` TCP connects.
Jon Patel: Can you paste the query/graph?
Maria Gomez: Query: `sum(rate(egress_bytes_total{pool=\"dedicated-eu-west\"}[1m])) by (tenant)` shows a sharp 3x bump for tenant=acme-upgrade.
Maria Gomez: Snip of logs:
```
2026-03-20T08:12:05Z SVC_HANDSHAKE tenant=acme-upgrade status=started conn_id=xyz
2026-03-20T08:12:05Z pool_assign tenant=acme-upgrade slot=warm-42
2026-03-20T08:12:05Z net_write tenant=acme-upgrade bytes=524288
2026-03-20T08:12:06Z SVC_HANDSHAKE tenant=acme-upgrade status=retry conn_id=xyz tries=3
```
Priya Singh: :eyes: looks like handshake retries + large initial payloads (524k) — could be a client-side aggressive reconnect + kv-cache regen pulling big prefixes.
Alex Chen: Are these TLS handshakes or application handshakes? We saw similar pattern when our client SDK did prefetch + reconnect loop.
Maria Gomez: Application-level handshake. The `net_write` is the cache prefetch stream right after assign.
Jon Patel: If the warm-slot prefetch is unbounded it can amplify egress when many handoffs happen simultaneously. Any correlation with maintenance or scaling events?
Maria Gomez: There was a rolling drain for 2 nodes in eu-west at 08:10. Warm-pool refills around 08:12 triggered a batch of reassigns.
Priya Singh: Hypothesis: drain -> many tenants get reassigned -> clients reconnect -> warm-slot prefetch all fire -> egress spike -> noisy neighbor effect on rack egress.
Alex Chen: Probable. Short-term mitigations: 1) Add jitter to prefetch start, 2) throttle prefetch bandwidth per-tenant, 3) rate-limit handshake retries at the proxy.
Jon Patel: Agree. Also consider delaying full prefetch until steady-state for new warm slots (TTL 30s -> 2m).
Maria Gomez: Can we flip a canary that adds 150-300ms randomized jitter to `prefetch.start()` in the runtime for eu-west only?
Priya Singh: Yup. I can push a config override to stencil for eu-west warm-pool: `warm_prefetch_jitter_ms: 150-300` and `prefetch_bandwidth_limit_kbps: 2000` as a canary.
Jon Patel: Add a proxy knob: `handshake_retry_backoff_ms` from 100 -> 400 with jitter. That should collapse the retry storms.
Maria Gomez: I'll open a short-lived incident doc and add metrics to monitor: per-tenant egress, handshake rate, prefetch bytes/sec, rack egress util.
ops-alert-bot: Incident created: I-2026-330-eu-west-egress-prefetch (owner: Maria Gomez).
Alex Chen: Quick checklist: 1) deploy staging runtime jitter, 2) push stencil override to eu-west, 3) ramp proxy backoff, 4) run a synthetic handoff load to validate.
Priya Singh: I'll do (2) and (3) now, will post rollout logs.
Maria Gomez: Thanks — set alert thresholds to 2.5x baseline for egress per-tenant and rack-level 80% egress util.
Jon Patel: If canary looks good, we'll schedule a global policy for warm-pool refill smoothing.
Maria Gomez: Filed infra issue: `ENG-xyz-agg-telemetry-prefetch-throttle` with next steps.
Priya Singh: Rollout update: override applied to eu-west at 08:42 UTC, watch dashboard.
Maria Gomez: Dashboard shows egress peak down ~65% vs spike baseline. Looks promising. :tada:
Jon Patel: Nice. Follow-up: we should add a postmortem-style blurb to the rollout notes so product teams know warm-prefetch can impact egress.
Maria Gomez: Agreed — I'll add to the incident doc and ping solutions for customer comms if needed.
Alex Chen: Great work, team.
Maria Gomez: Closing thread updates once the global policy PR is merged.
